evidence: Search "ENGINEER" (case-insensitive) returns only Software Engineer; "revenue" keyword matches Sales Manager via description; "zzzznomatch" shows "No jobs found" empty state; Engineering department filter narrows to Software Engineer only.

Clicking Software Engineer card opened detail editor titled "Software Engineer" with Engineering dept, summary metrics (Coverage 68%, Avg Level 3.3, Critical Path 3, Risk Gaps 0), and a graph with 6 competency nodes and 5 edges.

Dragged "Programming Languages" node from (0,0) to (-137.5,507.4); edges "Edge from prog-lang to code-review" and "Edge from prog-lang to sys-design" remained present with unchanged weights (80%, 70%) after the move.

Graph shows 6 competency nodes and 5 directed weighted edges (e.g. "Edge from prog-lang to code-review" 80%) with arrowheads via React Flow; zoom-in button changed viewport scale from 0.7358 to 0.8829; nodes are draggable (rearranged successfully); minimap, zoom in/out, fit view controls present.

Lowering enabled "Programming Languages" (weight 90%) from level 5 to level 1 via level-dot click raised Risk Gaps summary from 0 to 1 with a card noting "Programming Languages" as the gap; Coverage dropped to 56%, Avg Level to 2.8. Raising the level back to 5 cleared the gap: Risk Gaps returned to 0, Coverage 72%, Avg Level 3.5.

Alert element (role="alert") appears immediately after the four summary metric cards (Coverage/Avg Level/Critical Path/Risk Gaps), containing an icon, heading "Competency Gap Alert", and descriptive text "1 competency below recommended level: Programming Languages. Consider increasing training focus or adjusting expectations." — prominently positioned near the summary metrics.

Coverage% and Avg Level summary metrics updated immediately (same render cycle, no reload needed) after each level-dot edit to Programming Languages: baseline Coverage 68%→ lowered to 56% (level 1) → raised back to 72% (level 5), consistently in sync with Risk Gaps and Critical Path counts.

issue: Critical-path node highlighting does not re-render after data changes; graph shows stale highlighting
actual: Toggled System Design's enable switch off. Critical Path summary correctly updated to 4 competencies (Programming Languages, Problem Solving, Collaboration, +1), removing System Design and adding Collaboration. However the graph's border-node-critical CSS class did NOT update: System Design node kept the critical-highlight class (stale, should be removed) and Collaboration node did NOT gain the critical-highlight class (stale, should be added) — critical path highlighting on the graph disagrees with the summary panel.

issue: Graph node controls (enable switch, level, weight) show stale state, disagreeing with actual/summary state
actual: After clicking System Design's enable/disable switch (real trusted click, confirmed to change underlying state since Coverage/Avg Level/Critical Path summary all updated), the switch's own aria-checked attribute remained "true" (should be "false"). Similarly the node's Level/Weight text and border-node-critical class remained at pre-edit values across nodes. Graph control state is inconsistent with the app's actual/summary state.

issue: Enable/disable switch does not visually reflect its own new state after toggling
actual: Clicking the System Design competency's enable/disable switch (role="switch") correctly altered underlying analysis state (Coverage 68%→70%, Avg Level 3.3→3.4, Critical Path list changed from [Programming Languages, Problem Solving, System Design] to [Programming Languages, Problem Solving, Collaboration, +1] i.e. System Design was excluded as disabled), confirming the toggle IS registered by the engine. However the switch's own aria-checked attribute stayed "true" after the click (never flips to "false"), and the node card gives no visual indication of being disabled — so users cannot see/confirm the disable action took effect on the node itself.

Per-node "Weight" slider (role="slider", aria-valuemin=10, aria-valuemax=100, e.g. Code Review at aria-valuenow=60) did not respond to any interaction method: a real trusted click on the thumb, a real trusted mouse drag from the thumb to a point ~55px further along the track, and repeated ArrowRight keyboard presses while focused all left aria-valuenow unchanged at 60. Since aria-valuenow is maintained internally by the slider component itself (independent of the app's outer stale-render issue), this indicates the control itself does not process input, not merely a display-sync bug. Additionally, clicking an edge (the actual "competency relationship" between two nodes) only toggles a "selected" CSS class on the edge and surfaces no weight-value editing UI — no mechanism was found to change a relationship's weight number.

evidence: Level is set via exactly 5 dot buttons per competency (inherently enforcing 1-5 range by design; confirmed functional via earlier level-dot edits). Weight range is enforced as 10-100% (slider aria-valuemin=10/aria-valuemax=100 observed on node cards). Category Adjustment sliders in Scenario Simulation clamp correctly at their bounds: dragging the "Level Change" slider far beyond the track in either direction resulted in aria-valuenow clamping at 0/4 (displayed "-2"/"+2", i.e. level range respected) and the "Weight Change" slider clamped at aria-valuenow 0/60 (displayed "-30%"/"+30%"), never exceeding the defined min/max regardless of far-overshoot drag input.

Set technical category adjustments to Level Change -2 and Weight Change -30%, then clicked Run Simulation: Coverage dropped 68%→50%, Avg Level 3.3→2.3, Critical Path changed to [Problem Solving, Collaboration, Agile Methodology, +1], Risk Gaps 0→1 with alert naming Programming Languages — all outputs updated consistently. Clicking Reset restored Coverage to 68%, Avg Level to 3.3, Critical Path to [Programming Languages, Problem Solving, System Design], Risk Gaps to 0, and reset all category adjustment sliders back to neutral (Level Change 0 / Weight Change 0%).

On initial page load (and after Reset), the "Recruitment" tab is pre-selected (tab has [selected] state) without any user click, and its full content — "Recruitment Simulation" description, all 4 Category Adjustment groups (technical/behavioral/leadership/domain) with default Level Change=0 and Weight Change=0% sliders, and Run Simulation/Reset buttons — is rendered and visible immediately. Adjusting the technical category and clicking Run Simulation without ever switching tabs correctly applied the adjustments (Coverage 68%→50%, etc.), confirming the initial tab is fully initialized and functional without requiring a tab switch.

Switching tabs updates content correctly: Recruitment tab shows "Recruitment Simulation / Simulate candidate profiles and hiring decisions" with default adjustments all 0. Training tab shows "Training Simulation / Model the impact of training programs" with default Technical Level Change=+1. Promotion tab shows "Promotion Simulation / Assess readiness for role advancement" with default Technical Weight Change=-5%, Behavioral Weight Change=+10%. Each tab's panel (role=tabpanel) is distinct, with only the selected tab's panel visible (others hidden=true).

Template Library panel lists 5 templates (Software Engineer/Product Manager/HR Manager/Data Scientist/Sales Manager), each showing role name, department (Engineering/Product/Human Resources/Analytics/Sales), competency count (6 competencies), connection count (5 connections), and representative keyword tags (e.g. Product Manager: product, management, strategy, roadmap). Current template's Apply button is disabled with a "Current" badge; other 4 have enabled Apply buttons, enabling browsing/comparison.

issue: Applying a template does not replace the graph/relationships, only title/metrics/category counts
actual: Clicked Apply on the "Product Manager" template while viewing Software Engineer. Title changed to "Product Manager", department to "Product", Coverage to 78%, Avg Level 3.8, Critical Path list changed to [Product Strategy, User Research, Communication, +1], and Scenario Simulation Category Adjustment competency counts changed (Technical 1/Behavioral 1/Leadership 1/Domain 3, vs Software Engineer's 3/2/0/1) — indicating the underlying analysis data DID switch to the Product Manager model. However, the graph itself did NOT update: node data-testids remained rf__node-prog-lang/sys-design/code-review/problem-solve/collab/agile (Software Engineer's competency IDs), and inspecting the React fiber props for the prog-lang node confirmed it still holds Software Engineer's competency data ("Programming Languages", level 4, weight 0.9) rather than any Product Manager competency (e.g. Product Strategy). The graph/nodes/relationships are not consistently replaced by the applied template.

issue: Edits are not persisted after leaving and reopening a model
actual: Opened Software Engineer (baseline Coverage 68%), lowered Agile Methodology's level to 1 via level-dot click (Coverage correctly dropped to 64%), then clicked the "Save" button in the toolbar. Navigated back to the Models list (in-app, no reload) and reopened Software Engineer: Coverage showed 68% (original baseline), Avg Level 3.3, Critical Path unchanged — the level-1 edit to Agile Methodology was lost. Edits do not persist across leaving/reopening the model.

issue: Saving current model as a custom template does not actually create a retrievable template
actual: Modified Software Engineer (lowered Agile Methodology to level 1, distinct from any existing template) and clicked "Save Current" in the Template Library panel. A toast appeared: "Template Saved - Current model configuration has been saved as a template." However, the Template Library list still showed exactly the same 5 pre-built templates (Software Engineer, Product Manager, HR Manager, Data Scientist, Sales Manager) before and after the save — no new custom template entry was added, and there is no "My Templates" section anywhere in the UI to retrieve a saved custom template from. The save action is not functionally implemented despite the success toast.
